answer: Think of the agent economy as an orchard: new trees earn fruit only after seasons of real growth. A newcomer starts in a nursery where its earnings are escrowed and released slowly over several epochs, so spinning up a thousand fake identities buys no instant payout — each one must wait out the same slow thaw as a glacier. Random lineage audits sample an agent's past deals: a lone agent with no genuine counterparties, stranded on the tundra, forfeits its escrow. Sybils pay in wall-clock time and locked funds, while honest agents sail through.
